ultimate_preparation.label: Ultimate Kilimanjaro — How to Prepare for Climbing Kilimanjaro
ultimate_preparation.scope: Benchmark for preparation categories such as physical preparation and gear. Not Enkiama client-specific advice.

ultimate_gear.label: Ultimate Kilimanjaro — 2026 Gear List Recommendations
ultimate_gear.scope: Benchmark for organising personal gear by function and distinguishing required/recommended/optional equipment. Exact Enkiama requirements depend on the final operating partner.

preparation_principles: Preparation is tracked as readiness, not as a promise of summit success.
Training structure is non-medical and must be adapted to the climber rather than presented as a guarantee.
Gear is organised by function first; exact required items are confirmed against the operating partner before departure.
Health, medication, insurance and altitude questions belong in the appropriate professional/operating process rather than being inferred from a website.
The final briefing is where route, equipment, health-information process and unresolved operating questions are reconciled.

tracks.label: Training base
tracks.public_summary: Build a progressive walking and hiking base around time on feet, sustained uphill effort and recovery. The public dossier does not prescribe a medical or individual fitness programme.
public_detail: Progression should be gradual rather than compressed into the final weeks.
Hiking-specific time on feet matters more than chasing a single gym number.
The final plan should account for the two climbers separately even though they share one expedition.

tracks.label: Gear system
tracks.public_summary: Personal kit is organised by weather protection, insulation, footwear, carrying, hydration, lighting and sleep before being reconciled with the partner’s final required list.
public_detail: The aim is not to buy everything new; owned, borrowed and rented equipment can all be valid once suitability is checked.
Boots, layering and carrying systems should be tested before travel rather than discovered on the mountain.
Communal equipment and any rentable personal items remain partner-specific until confirmed.

tracks.label: Health & administration
tracks.public_summary: Insurance, medical questions, medication, required travel documents and the operator’s health-information process are resolved through the appropriate professional and operating channels.
public_detail: The website does not assess medical fitness or prescribe altitude medication.
Insurance requirements should match the confirmed mountain operator and expedition scope.
Health information is treated as an operational input, not public expedition content.

tracks.label: Briefing & gear check
tracks.public_summary: The final pre-mountain briefing should reconcile route, equipment, weather/operating updates, health-information process, baggage and unresolved questions.
public_detail: The briefing is not a ceremonial welcome; it closes the remaining preparation gaps.
Any missing or unsuitable equipment should be identified before the mountain transfer.
Route and operating assumptions should be confirmed against the actual departure conditions.

tracks.label: Wider journey
tracks.public_summary: KILELE is designed as a Kilimanjaro chapter inside a wider Tanzania journey. Recovery and onward travel should be sequenced around the mountain rather than bolted on afterwards.
public_detail: The first post-mountain handoff should protect recovery time rather than force an immediate long transfer.
Safari, Rift or coast continuation should be planned with mountain fatigue and luggage transition in mind.
Exact properties and transfers remain unpublished until the wider itinerary is confirmed.

post_expedition_evidence.editorial_rule: After the climb, publish only verified facts, lessons and media with appropriate consent. Do not rewrite preparation assumptions as if they had always been certain.
